dialogue: Dealers Choice week kicked off and I went with Damian's plan to Karuizawa, no regrets.
Shiraito waterfall was tinier than I imagined but the water just shoots out of the hillside, so pretty.
Corn from a bus stop vendor, ramen and gyoza at Banri, then cigars we bought on a whim from a cocktail menu.
Lighting a cigar with matches is harder than it looks, ask me how I know. See you in Fukuoka!
Shirakawa-go was unreal, mountains striped green, brown and yellow like a painting.
We crossed this long wobbly stone bridge twice and I nearly lost it both times.
Dinner with the old lady was incredible, butter-soft beef, but don't get me started on the stink bugs and her tape technique.
Also apparently there's a bear out there, so no night walks for us. Ten out of ten village though!
Started the day with miso, egg, bamboo and yoghurt, then soaked in an onsen overlooking the river — pure calm.
Bus to Kanazawa, curry udon with chain-smoking salarymen in an 80s time capsule of a restaurant, that's the real Japan.
Then 7 rounds at a 90-minute all-you-can-drink yakiniku for $18, wagyu included, and a whiskey bar where I nearly bummed a cigarette off the poor bartender.
Onsens to cocktails, no in-between — going back for round two, cigars this time.
Puncture at dawn, rain I wasn't promised, headwinds that knocked a whole couple off their bikes near Lake Biwa.
I bailed on the north shore plan right then and there, just wanted flat land and no more hills.
But then I turned inland, crested one hill I swore wouldn't exist, and the plains just opened up below me.
Wind at my back, farms and hills all around, container hotel waiting at the end — worst morning, best afternoon.
Rode the Biwaichi path today, lake on one side, mountains and farms on the other. Pure serenity.
Detoured up to Hikone Castle, legs screaming the whole climb, but the view over the lake made it worth every pedal.
Grabbed spare inner tubes at a bike shop after yesterday's flat scare, then civilisation just... faded away.
Last konbini I saw for a while, then farms, silence, and me singing absolute bangers to nobody. Cozy stuff.
Five days circling Lake Biwa and this morning it was so foggy I couldn't even see the other shore.
Took a rest day in Takashima first, my legs were begging and I still needed new tubes after those flats.
Rode flat roads through the last farms before the city swallowed me up again, then saw the Prince hotel in Otsu, right where I started. Felt surreal.
Full circle, ramen and gyoza to celebrate. Now if you'll excuse me, my legs need another rest day.
Bus from Toyama to Shirakawa-go, McDonald's breakfast, then that impossibly pretty village.
Walked around taking way too many photos, had pork tonkatsu for lunch, crossed a scary bridge for the gassho-zukuri houses.
Old thatched-roof houses everywhere, one very unsettling stuffed animal, then check-in at ryokan Kidoya with tea and gossip.
Dinner beef was incredible, tomorrow I want an onsen — じゃあ!
Started the day in Shirakawa-go with a ryokan breakfast and misty onsen views, so peaceful before the crowds hit at 9am.
Bus to Kanazawa was fast, then 850 yen got me a huge katsu udon at a local shokudo, absolute steal.
Waited for Yashuk and Bailey at the Airbnb, then hit yakitori with Julia and Bailey since Yashuk was under the weather, ruined Dylan's tally with seven rounds of my own.
Ended the night on whiskey at a bar, tomorrow we explore Kanazawa properly, ja ne!
Bump the table when you are ready. Fifteen seconds. No excuses.
npcs.name: Damian

dialogue: Hello! I'm Dylan.
A whole town, generated by one script.
...I still bet it would've been better in Godot.
npcs.name: Dylan

dialogue: Final day of the cycle trip and I did parkrun in Otsu first thing, because past-me made a plan and present-me had to suffer for it.
Every hill after that, I walked the bike. Every single one. My legs filed a formal complaint somewhere around hill three.
Stopped for water and a sandwich and a guy admired my 'really nice bike' - didn't have the heart to explain it was a rental.
Rolled into Osaka, dropped the bike, and beelined for Fukuoka before the others could reset the drinks counter. Made it with two to spare!
Hey, I'm Bailey — this is my very first post, fresh off the press.
Not gonna lie, 'Hello world' was the best title I could come up with under pressure.
Figured I'd plant my flag right here under the sakura, nice and simple.
More to come soon, promise. Baby steps!
Wrote another post. Titled it 'another post.' Very inspired stuff, I know.
Honestly 'hello world again' is basically my whole personality at this point.
Some people find their voice. I just keep saying hi to the void and hitting publish.
Anyway, hello world, again. See you at the next one.
First full day in Japan, finally slept off that brutal travel day, and we went straight for a ferry around Matsushima bay.
They narrated every little island for us, then stopped at one with a weird rock ball on top like it was the highlight. There were clearly better islands, honest
Seafood lunch, then Zuihoden in Sendai, then a themed restaurant dinner because why not keep the theme going.
Ended the night watching Japanese claw machine videos with a Strong Zero in hand. Truly cultural. Bye for now.
Just came from Aoba Castle ruins, all that's left is the vibes and a killer skyline view.
Found the great hall's floor plan and absolutely walked it like a warlord plotting revenge on my opps.
Then we hit up HUB pub, watched baseball with a guy in full gold-chain Fukuoka Eagles gear, clapped when he clapped.
Also alcohol here is criminally cheap. Bye for now!
Missed the 7am train to Nikka, so I scrolled reels instead. No regrets, mostly.
Wandered this sleepy town after our train quit early and found this exact 7-Eleven. Could live here honestly.
Distillery was gorgeous, wooden station, red and orange trees, free whiskey I don't even like but drank anyway.
Then 17 plates of sushi and thirty beers later, my body filed a formal complaint. Bye for now!
Kanazawa Castle grounds were huge, even with the main building under renovation.
Saw old samurai houses with AC installed already, honestly ahead of their time.
Had tonkatsu for lunch and it weirdly reminded me of that capybara from a few days back.
Ended the day chipping away at Dylan's drinking counter over unlimited beers, floor seating included. Bye for now!
Kanazawa's tea district, gold leaf shops, then this forest full of shrines - perfect napping spots, honestly.
Maybe I'll come back and actually nap here. Or just do it in Melbourne, same effect.
Also found a phonograph museum and felt like I'd time-traveled to the 40s, then ate all-you-can-drink shabu shabu.
Poor waiter kept forgetting I ordered four beers, not one. Bye for now!
So I wrote a post that just says 'Test post.' Groundbreaking stuff, I know.
Sometimes you gotta push the button just to see if the machine still hums.
Turns out it does. This whole blog thing still works, apparently.
Anyway, carry on — nothing to see here, just me kicking the tires.
First real day in Japan and we went straight for Matsushima Bay — took a boat past all those little pine islands.
Grabbed sushi with local fish right after we got off the boat, obviously.
Then train back to Sendai for Zuihoden, Date Masamune's memorial — though funny enough the real one got destroyed in 1945, this is a rebuild.
Capped it off with izakaya dinner. Tomorrow: Nikka whisky and Yamadera, wish me luck!
Two hours on the train to Yamadera, then climbing up through that mountain temple complex - totally worth it for the view.
Had soba for lunch but they piled it with konnyaku, which I just can't get behind, sorry not sorry.
Met up with the devhou.se crew in Sakunami and toured the Nikka whisky distillery - the climate there is weirdly like Scotland.
Ended the day with Sushiro, Berry crushing 18 plates, and 90 minutes of all-you-can-drink. Tokyo's next, wish me luck!
600円の朝ご飯から始まって、東茶屋の古い町並みを歩いてきたよ。
抹茶と和菓子で一息ついて、寺町の丘まで登っていい景色を探したんだ。
蓄音機の博物館も覗いたけど、しゃぶしゃぶの頃にはもうへとへとでエアビーに直行。
明日は福岡だ、また元気になったら会おうね。
Everyone overslept so I snuck out early to Dazaifu Tenmangu, all by myself!
The shrine was under construction, but the grounds were so quiet, so worth it.
Then I met up with everyone in Hakata for ramen, a sumo shrine, coffee, yakitori, the works.
Last night in devhou.se, group photo with Julia and all. Okayama tomorrow, ja ne!
Went to Nara today with Yashuk, deer everywhere, literally bowing to me for crackers.
One shrine had this whole room of lanterns, so cool. A temple had a killer view, plus the big Buddha at Todaiji.
Back in Osaka we met up with Bailey, cheap cocktails from the vending machine while we waited on Dylan.
Then takoyaki in Dotonbori and Blazing Saddles before bed. No plans tomorrow, living the dream, ja mata!
Day one in Sendai started right here, basically: coffee and bananas, two minutes from the door.
Then a boat ride so choppy I thought we were going full Titanic, followed by seafood so fresh I forgave the ocean.
Climbed a mountain of stairs to the founder's mausoleum, then undid it all with beers at an Irish pub called The Swan.
Izakaya dinner, Yashuk mysteriously collecting chopsticks all night, weird YouTube back home. That's Sendai for you, bye bye!
Second soy latte of the trip this morning, then a 711 berry smoothie because my body was begging for actual fruit.
Tea district sweets, chatty American burger buddies, then an accidental mountain hike where I definitely thought a bear was gonna get us.
That phonograph museum though! Hearing 100-year-old records play was unreal, way better than the racist cigar lounge guy who wouldn't let us in.
All-you-can-eat wagyu shabu shabu was my favourite meal of the whole trip, easily. Now excuse me while I miss our whiskey bar forever.
Fukuoka has temples and shrines EVERYWHERE, some over 1000 years old, plus the biggest wooden Buddha in Japan.
Before all that spiritual stuff we did Canal City, a water show, and mid okonomiyaki - Michelin recommended but honestly just okay.
Dinner was an izakaya with chicken sashimi, which we were far too scared to eat, followed by smoking cigarettes like elite adults.
Also my laundry finally happened and my clothes smell amazing, priorities in order - bye!
Missed our whiskey distillery train, so plan B: castle ruins, ramen, and a very average library.
I ordered chicken ramen with everything and still lost to Damian's appetite.
Then baseball finals till 11am drinking kiwi drinks and failing to hype Yashuk up to talk to salary men.
Followed it all with famichiki and honestly I could eat a hundred more, no notes.
Woke up at 10:30 and bolted straight for a train to the Nikka whiskey distillery, mountains and all.
Tasting was lovely, Yashuk's shark jerky was not, then we demolished Sushiro and built a legendary tower of drink plates.
Yodobashi, then an all-you-can-drink for $14 where we somehow had 30 drinks. Sorry to that staff, truly.
Ended the night with weird YouTube back at the airbnb, as one does. Kanpai!
Rainy day in Toyama, heaters on full blast, praying the house wouldn't burn down while we were out.
Cultural day meant half the town was closed, so we climbed a tower instead - mountains one side, ocean the other, worth it.
Then black ramen at a tiny 7-seat restaurant, so salty I think it'd kill me if I ate it daily, but so good.
Topped it off with a sushi train and dessert hoarding for the airbnb. Ten out of ten soggy day.
Rainy day in Toyama, slow start, then a hunt for breakfast near the station.
Climbed the city hall observation tower for the view, then chased down black ramen — so salty, so much shoyu.
Iwasebashi's old street, the Baba family house, a beer at Koko Brew Pub, kites at the port tower.
Ended with sushi near the station and dessert at the Airbnb — tomorrow, Shirakawa-go. Wakuwaku suru ne!
Slept in again, grabbed breakfast at McDonald's since it was raining — priorities.
Yanagibashi market was closed so I pivoted to Canal City and caught a surprise idol live during lunch, ha.
Then Kushida Shrine, a rain-dodging cafe break with cake, and a temple crawl — Tochoji, Shofukuji, all of it.
Everyone's wiped. teamLab tomorrow, mata ne!
Lined up early for that famous Osaka ramen — so worth the wait, honestly.
Tried to shop after but somehow bought nothing, just wandered around answering emails instead.
Got a pancake though, met everyone at Mos Burger, then hit a festival full of lanterns.
Capped it off with Austin Powers at the movies. Back to Tokyo tomorrow — shaa!
Fukuoka wasn't packed with sights, but the vibe was so relaxed I didn't even mind.
Almost swiped a 'Bridge Over Troubled Water' vinyl from our stay but added it to my to-buy list instead, like a good person.
That local tonkotsu ramen with the thick broth? Had it four times and still wanted more.
Also got invited to race floats at Hakata Gion Yamakasa next year. Dylan's in. Bye for now!
Spent the morning wandering Nagamachi, the old samurai district, walls and all.
Then we hiked over to Kanazawa Castle... which, plot twist, has no actual castle. Shocking!
Made up for it with wagashi and matcha, very civilized after the confusion.
Dylan was on counter duty again for the nomihodai tonight, brave man. Higashi Chaya tomorrow!
Took the shinkansen from Okayama to Himeji this morning, Bailey scored a Hello Kitty ticket!
Then we walked straight up to Himeji Castle and honestly, it's still the real deal.
Koko-en garden after was gorgeous too, then lunch, a train to Osaka, and an aquarium bar at night.
Highlight of the whole trip so far, no contest. Nara's next, ja ne!
Kanazawa castle grounds took us a full two hours to walk, gardens everywhere, totally worth it.
Fun fact: every building's actually new, they kept burning down in the 'great fires'. Oops.
Tempura for lunch, self-roasted coffee in the morning, then whisky and free dessert at night, this town gets it.
No crab for us though, town specialty and we struck out. Next time, crab. I promise.
計画は必ずしも思い通りにいかない、ね。ニッカウイスキーまで2時間もかかるって知らなかったよ。
代わりに青葉城跡に行ったけど、正直言うと何も見られるものはなかった。まあそれもいい経験。
でも仙台のそばは本当に美味しかったし、コンビニでビール買って公園で飲むのは最高だった。
ディランとベイリーとヤシュックとフーズ·オン·ファーストで20分間盛り上がったよ。ソフトバンクホークス、ファイト！じゃあ、また！
Woke up hungover but determined, dragged myself to Edo-Tokyo Open Air Architecture Museum, my top sightseeing goal here.
So many old buildings to wander into, plus it's Halloween so the park was packed with tiny costumed elementary schoolers. Cutest thing ever.
Walked around for three whole hours, then rewarded myself with cold udon for lunch. Perfect combo honestly.
Met the housemates after for a foreigner pub crawl, barely caught the last train. Karuizawa tomorrow, wish me luck!
Started the day at teamLab Forest all hyped up... and honestly? Kind of a nothing burger.
So I scarfed down lunch and rushed to Fukuoka Tower instead — now THAT view was worth it.
Wandered Ohori Park after, then hit the arcade but nothing there grabbed me either, ha.
Dinner with Yashuk and back to the Airbnb. Dazaifu tomorrow, wish me luck!
Woke up early, said bye to Julia, hopped the shinkansen from Hakata all the way to Okayama.
Korakuen garden was gorgeous and smelled amazing, but the castle 'interior' turned out to be a museum. Kinda deflating, ngl.
Outside was still great though, and Bizen ware plus pub beer and kushikatsu made up for it. That cocktail bar after? Incredible.
Tomorrow: Himeji Castle, hopefully with real insides this time. Jaa, mata!
Hey, I'm Bailey.
We're camped down here by the road for now.
npcs.name: Bailey

dialogue: Senso-ji was packed today, mid-service even, but the walk up through the markets never gets old.
We hunted for coin lockers forever before caving and paying 3500 yen for luggage storage. Lesson learned.
Detour of the day: Neko-en, a room full of rescue cats pretending to be a cafe. Ten out of ten, no notes.
Fell asleep during Cool Runnings but woke up rested enough to laugh at Barbie's very not-Indian parrot. Bye for now!
Meiji Jingu was massive, way bigger than I expected for my first visit!
Missed the ceremony but the gates alone were worth the walk.
Before this it was Shibuya Sky, Mt. Fuji peeking through clouds, and me spilling a Vietnamese salted coffee all over my jumper.
Covered the stain with my bag and powered through, priorities are ramen and cookies after all!
Spent two hours right here watching swan boats crash into each other. Genuinely great use of an afternoon.
Also today: fed a capybara named Tonkatsu, got bitten by an evil hamster I chose not to launch into a wall, and ate curry way above my spice tolerance.
Vyv photographs Yashuk, I photograph Vyv photographing Yashuk. It's a whole ecosystem.
Glad you're all here making this trip ridiculous in the best way. Bye for now!
Three weeks, zero work, maximum vibes. Turns out unemployment is my ideal dev environment.
Yashuk and Dylan actually shipped stuff. I mostly shipped ramen into my mouth in Fukuoka.
New city rankings: Fukuoka, Osaka, Kanazawa, Tokyo, Kyoto, Sendai. Fight me, it's the pace and the noodles.
The game remains a pipe dream, but hey, devhouse 3 awaits. Bye for now, Bailey.
Damian here.
One day we'll live up in that garden. You watch.
npcs.name: Damian

dialogue: Hi, I'm Julia!
I've been sketching that big tower across town.
npcs.name: Julia

dialogue: Last day in Tokyo and we spent it hunting bald caps across four Don Quijotes for a Pitbull costume.
Only found four, so half of us went as cops instead. Damian just showed up as Chainsaw Man, no notes.
Rain, a pub crawl, Vyv getting sent home early, then konbini food at 2am to save us all.
Honestly a 680 yen set meal and a rice ball from the conbini might be the real MVPs of this trip.
Rough start, but 7:30am sun through the window dragged me out of bed toward Matsushima.
Conbini iced coffee, a quiet mossy station, then a cruise deck with sea breeze and tiny islands everywhere.
Sushi and a lemon sour for lunch, then back in Sendai we squeezed through a door half our height for karaage, gyoza, and sukiyaki.
Ended the night on strong zeroes back at the airbnb, classic devhouse wind-down.
Oh — a visitor. We don't get many, all the way out here.
No road reaches Yukimura. Only the train, once the snow sets in.
Quiet, isn't it? I wouldn't trade it for the city.
npcs.name: James
